title: Zero dimensional scheme theoretic stabilizers give finite orbit torsors
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let it act on a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $x\in X(k)$ let $H$ be the scheme-theoretic stabilizer, representing $R\mapsto\{g\in G(R):gx_R=x_R\}$, and let $O_x\subset X$ be the locally closed orbit with its reduced subscheme structure [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry]. The following are equivalent: $\dim H=0$; $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite; and the set $H(k)$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. When they hold, the orbit map $\beta_x:G\to O_x$ is finite locally free and surjective [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. More precisely $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$ is an isomorphism $G\times_kH\simeq G\times_{O_x}G$, so $\beta_x$ is an $H$-torsor for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. Dimension is Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; no reducedness or smoothness of $H$, and no reducedness of $X$, is assumed.

source.place: Section 2.14, printed p.44 (finite algebraic group schemes), Propositions 7.4, 7.11--7.12 and 7.15, printed pp.139--143 (orbit as quotient and finite flat quotient map). Zero-dimensional finite-type schemes: Stacks varieties.tex Tag 06LH, lemma-algebraic-scheme-dim-0; finite locally free descent: descent.tex Tag 02VO, lemma-descending-property-finite-locally-free. Finite k-points imply dimension zero by the Jacobson/Nullstellensatz property over algebraically closed k.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry], $H$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $G$, $O_x$ is smooth and locally closed, and $\beta_x:G\to O_x$ is faithfully flat. Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $H=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B=A/I$. Since $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, so is $B$: the images of any algebra generators generate the quotient. The identity of $G$ fixes $x$, so $H$ is nonempty and $\dim H\geq0$.

source.place: Proposition 7.4(b) and the paragraph defining the isotropy group on printed p.140

proof.text: If $\dim H=0$ (topological Krull dimension), then by [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings] every local ring of $H$ has Krull dimension at most $0$, so $\dim H\le0$ in the sense of [def-pc-dimension]; apply [lem-pc-algebraic-dim-zero-affine-finite] to the finite-type scheme $H$ to obtain that $H\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is finite. Conversely, if that morphism is finite, [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives $\dim_k B<\infty$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] and [lem-sfb-artinian-spectrum-finite], $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is finite. Apply [pqf-lem-finite-type-algebra-finite-spectrum] to $B$: every prime is maximal and the spectrum is discrete, hence $\dim H=0$ since $H$ is nonempty.

Closed points of $H$ are exactly its $k$-points: [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] makes their residue fields equal to $k$ via the structure map, with a unique inverse, and the kernel of any $k$-algebra map $B\to k$ is maximal. Thus finite $H$ has finite $H(k)$ by step 2. Conversely, if $H(k)$ is finite, there are finitely many closed points. A nonclosed point would have infinitely many closed specializations by [lem-sc-finite-type-nonclosed-closure-closed-points], a contradiction. All points are therefore closed and the spectrum is finite; [pqf-lem-finite-type-algebra-finite-spectrum] again gives dimension zero. This proves all three equivalences, without discarding nilpotents.

source.place: Tag 0478, lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson; algebra.tex Tag 00FV, theorem-nullstellensatz, and Tag 0ALW

proof.text: The group operations give a morphism $\Phi:G\times_kH\to G\times_{O_x}G$, $(g,h)\mapsto(g,gh)$: $ghx=gx$ because $h$ fixes $x$. Define its inverse by $(g,g\prime)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}g\prime)$. The equality $gx=g\prime x$ implies $(g^{-1}g\prime)x=x$, so the second component factors through the representing stabilizer $H$. These are morphisms, obtained from multiplication, inversion and the universal properties of $H$ and the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], rather than a calculation only on $k$-points. Their composites are the identity because $g(g^{-1}g\prime)=g\prime$ and $g^{-1}(gh)=h$. Thus $\Phi$ is the claimed isomorphism over the first copy of $G$.

source.place: Propositions 7.11 and 7.15: the cartesian square, explicitly for the stabilizer

proof.text: We check the covering hypotheses independently of finiteness of $H$. The immersion $O_x\hookrightarrow X$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation], and its composite with the separated structure map of $X$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Since $G$ is finite type over $k$, [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target](b) gives that $\beta_x$ is finite type, in particular quasi-compact. Also $O_x$ is smooth over $k$ by step 1, hence locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Choose a covering of $O_x$ by affine spectra of Noetherian rings as in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Locally finite type for $\beta_x$ means that on affine charts over this covering its rings are finitely generated algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] they are finitely presented. This is local finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Thus $\beta_x$ is flat, surjective, quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation.

Assume the equivalent stabilizer conditions and put $n=\dim_k B$. The projection $G\times_kH\to G$ is finite: [lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change], with one summand and base ring $k$, identifies it with $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_kB)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ (interchange the tensor factors if necessary). A $k$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ of $B$ makes $1\otimes b_1,\ldots,1\otimes b_n$ an $A$-basis, so this is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Step 4 identifies it with the base change of $\beta_x$ along itself, using the first projection. Step 5 verifies flatness, surjectivity and quasi-compactness of that covering map. Apply [lem-sbc-finite-morphism-fpqc-descent] to conclude that $\beta_x$ is finite. Its flatness and local finite presentation have already been proved, so [def-pc-finite-locally-free] makes it finite locally free; surjectivity is step 1.

Right multiplication defines the $H$-action on $G$ over $O_x$. Pulling back by the covering $\beta_x:G\to O_x$, step 4 gives the equivariant trivialization $G\times_{O_x}G\simeq G\times_kH$. Under it, the section is $(g,1)$, and right multiplication in the second factor is the given action. The cover is faithfully flat and finitely presented: local finite presentation is step 5, quasi-compactness follows there (also from finiteness), and a finite morphism is affine, hence quasi-separated since on affine charts the diagonal is the closed immersion given by the surjection $C\otimes_R C\to C$. This verifies precisely the asserted torsor condition and the stipulated type of covering. At no point was $H$ replaced by its reduction.
